title: Machine Learning-Based Prognostic Prediction for Knee Osteoarthritis After High Tibial Osteotomy Using Wavelet-Derived Gait Features.
summary: Wavelet-derived gait features and machine learning were used to predict knee-osteoarthritis outcomes after high tibial osteotomy; predictions were assessed against follow-up clinical outcomes in the study cohort.
ai_technology: Machine-learning prognosis from wavelet-derived gait features after high tibial osteotomy.
organization: Department of Functional Reconstruction for the Knee Joint, Faculty of Medicine, Hokkaido University, Sapporo 060-8638, Japan

evidence.tested: Cohort-specific prediction evaluation against follow-up clinical outcomes; generalization beyond the studied cohort is unknown.
evidence.unknown: External replication and real-world or clinical benefit were not established by the reviewed study
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning prognosis from wavelet-derived gait features after high tibial osteotomy.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
